title: Woody Herman's manager and unpaid arrangements
summary: Kirchner recalls the Metronome piece; arrangements paid a token fee but never played.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Thinking back to that Metronome article that George Simon did in '46 that I was perusing the other day, that was written around the time that you had been with McKinley.
McKinley--they threw everybody out of the army at the end of '45 and that's when that started.
into that, there was something in that article about when you were with Woody and somehow the managers shafted you. Woody's manager--
Yes, it was mentioned that somehow you hadn't gotten paid properly for some of those arrangements, or something. I don't remember--
(Side B of Tape 3 ended at this point. Transcript will continue with Tape 4.)
--were not paid properly or something for some of those arrangements. I don't remember exactly.

Maybe I got fifty dollars or a hundred dollars, but they never played them. That was the problem. Why they kept asking for them I don't know. I wonder if Woody was even aware that they were there. I don't know that either. It was a pretty hot band at the time.
